question: Should OpenClaw add a broader config mode that disables URL tokens, HTTPS requirements, device identity, pairing, or tailnet trust checks for private deployments?
rationale: The request changes Gateway operator-auth and transport security boundaries; current source and docs expose narrower tokenless or delegated-auth paths but intentionally do not provide the full bypass requested here.

options.title: Keep Current Boundaries
options.body: Treat token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale Serve, and explicit break-glass paths as the supported surfaces and reject a blanket bypass.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Dangerous Mode
options.body: Design a named private-ingress or tailnet policy with explicit warnings, audit output, docs, startup checks, and tests instead of a generic urlToken switch.

options.title: Accept Broad External Trust
options.body: Allow self-managed deployments to disable multiple Gateway safeguards and rely on external network controls for operator access.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Boundaries
recommendation.body: Treat token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale Serve, and explicit break-glass paths as the supported surfaces and reject a blanket bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on Gateway auth hardening, Tailscale docs, and adjacent no-auth exposure fixes.
